findings.passage: Press accounts state that the Supreme Court may not rule on a case challenging an Indiana Voter ID law until June 2008. The law has already been upheld by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 7th Circuit. Opponents to the new law appealed on the basis that the new law causes mass disenfranchisement of certain voters. The law requires registered voters to show a government-issued photo identification card before they can cast a vote.
findings.note: Her blog post titled 'Voter ID', describing the Indiana photo-ID law case. Old post (2007), written while she was in the House.

findings.passage: Reasonable Voter ID Laws printed this week in the Washington Times makes great points about some of the opponents' illogical objections.
